newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia manufacturers ask for industry plan.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia manufacturers ask for industry plan.

text.p: The Australian Chamber of Manufactures (ACM) said on Wednesday the government needed to adopt a comprehensive industry plan if it was to maintain the economic contribution from the manufacturing sector.

"The objective is to halt and reverse the long-term decline in which manufacturing's share (of the economy) has fallen from 24 percent in 1970 to about 14.7 percent at present," chief executive Allan Handberg said in a statement.
He said the ACM called for the industry plan in its submission to the government-sponsored Mortimer review of Australian business programmes.
"Our objective is to boost manufacturing's confidence to invest in long-term growth and jobs," Handberg said.
Other targets set out in the ACM submission included:
-- a rise in exports to 40 percent of manufacturing sales by the year 2010, up from 28 percent currently;
-- annual manufacturing growth of at least three percent by 2010, up from about two percent at the moment; and
-- a rise in manufacturing investment to at least 20 percent of turnover by 2010, compared with an average of 15 percent over the past decade.
Handberg said the ACM also wanted the government to establish a business roundtable, to be chaired by the Prime Minister, to provide direct communication between the government and business.
It also called for a review of the taxation system, including the need for a consumption tax and simplification of fringe benefits tax.
"Australian manufacturing faces intensifying global competition in the period ahead," Handberg said.
"The challenge for the Australian government is to seize the opportunity to put in place a long-term plan for manufacturing growth, prosperity and jobs."
